transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-14
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Cole (CTO - Amplify), Lena Ortiz (ML Eng), Naoki Sato (DevOps), Ruth Park (PM)

Summary:
High-level scoping call for an inference pilot. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for a document processing / support-triage pipeline. Key concerns: p95 latency target, cost per 1M tokens, data residency/SOC2, KMS and SSO, and the timeline for a 4-6 week POC with benchmarks. Agreed next steps and action items.

Topics covered:
- Use case and success criteria
- Workload sizing and traffic profile
- Benchmark plan and metrics (latency, throughput, cost, quality)
- Deployment trade-offs: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
- Security/compliance checklist (SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs)
- Pilot timeline and decision gates

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Ellis: Hey everyone, uh thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood. Priya (SE) and I will run through a quick agenda — understand the use case, goals for the pilot, and then dig into hosting options.
[00:12] Marcus Cole: Hey Jordan, thanks. Marcus here, CTO at Amplify. We brought Lena and Naoki on to help with technical details. Ruth is on for product context.
[00:20] Ruth Park: Hi all.
[00:22] Priya Nair: Hi, quick agenda — 1) what you're trying to solve, 2) traffic/latency/cost targets, 3) propose pilot scope and runbook, 4) Q/A on security and deployment. Sound OK?
[00:30] Marcus Cole: Yup. Our main thing is we want to automate support triage across docs and emails. We need near real-time annotations — ideally p95 latency under 200ms for the short form requests, and under 500ms for longer analysis jobs. Throughput is variable, base is ~50 rps and peak-ish bursts to 300 rps during morning ingress windows.
[00:50] Lena Ortiz: To add, the models will see typical prompt lengths of 50-250 tokens; longest flows can be 1k tokens for context-heavy cases. We also care about model determinism for labels and having an eval that ensures we don't regress on ROUGE/F1.
[01:06] Naoki Sato: And on infra side we have EU data residency requirements; some PII must remain in our VPC. We're using GCP in europe-west1 with private peering to partners.
[01:18] Jordan Ellis: Great specifics — thanks. Priya, do you want to go through the hosting implications?
[01:22] Priya Nair: Sure. So shorthand: Hosted gives fastest time-to-value — we manage runtime, benchmarks, and elastic scaling. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and consistent tail latency and is good if you need throughput guarantees. Private (VPC or on-prem) is for customers with strict data residency or air-gap requirements. There are cost and ops trade-offs across each.
[01:40] Marcus Cole: For us the data residency + KMS controls push us toward either Dedicated inside our VPC or Private. But cost is real — we can't be 2-3x the cost of hosted, otherwise product economics break.
[01:52] Priya Nair: Right, and there are hybrid patterns: many customers start with Hosted for speed, run the benchmark workloads, then either move to Dedicated with VPC peering or deploy Private if regulations enforce it. You can also do model pinning and rollouts independent of the underlying environment.
[02:07] Lena Ortiz: Can we run the benchmark on Hosted but with synthetic data to test throughput, then run a small Dedicated pilot with real data behind our VPC?
[02:14] Jordan Ellis: Yes, that's a common pattern. For the POC we'd propose a staged plan: week 0-1 onboarding + test harness; week 2-3 benchmarks and quality evals on representative sets; week 4 decision/rollover to a Dedicated or Private pilot.
[02:27] Naoki Sato: What about latency — do you have numbers for 95th and 99th pcts for the different options?
[02:33] Priya Nair: We publish performance profiles per model. Ballpark: hosted with autoscale — p95 for short prompts ~100-180ms depending on model and q4 kernels; Dedicated on similar hardware can shave that down to 80-140ms p95 with stable tail latency because of reserved capacity. Private depends on your network egress and instance type; you can get close to Dedicated if the hardware and kernel stacks match. There is also the impact of batching and prefix/KV caching — if you have lots of similar prefixes you can drop per-token compute.
[02:59] Marcus Cole: We're also sensitive to cold starts. How does Redwood handle cold-cache and warmups?
[03:04] Priya Nair: We do proactive warm pools and keep KV caches alive for hot routes. Cold starts are minimized in Dedicated because the pool is reserved; hosted also has warm strategies but for very spiky workloads you'd want a burst buffer on Dedicated.
[03:18] Ruth Park: On success criteria — we'll need to avoid any regression in label accuracy, keep p95 under 200ms for 95% of flows, and keep cost per 1M tokens under an agreed threshold. Also a security review pass.
[03:29] Jordan Ellis: Makes sense. Let's make that explicit in the pilot success metrics. Priya, can you propose measurable gates?
[03:34] Priya Nair: Proposed POC gates: 1) Performance: p95 < 200ms for short-path workload, end-to-end including network; 2) Throughput: sustain 150 rps for 1 hour with acceptable p95; 3) Accuracy: automated eval — no more than 2% drop vs baseline on the provided prompt set; 4) Security: SOC2 docs provided, SAML SSO integrated in sandbox, KMS for key control; 5) Cost: directional estimate with expected per-token spend within X% of hosted benchmark.
[04:03] Lena Ortiz: We'll run our evaluation harness and compute F1/precision/recall per label. We'll share the scripts.
[04:09] Marcus Cole: About KMS — we use Cloud KMS with customer-managed keys. Can Redwood integrate?
[04:14] Priya Nair: Yes, Redwood supports KMS integration for Private and Dedicated; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed keys via HSM integrations for enterprise tiers. We'll send the KMS integration guide.
[04:25] Naoki Sato: And SSO? We use SAML with Okta.
[04:28] Jordan Ellis: We support SAML/SSO and RBAC. We'll include steps in the runbook.
[04:33] Marcus Cole: Any audit logging — we need end-to-end request logs retained for 90 days in EU.
[04:38] Priya Nair: Audit logs are configurable; retention is an add-on in Hosted, included in Dedicated/Private depending on contract. We'll document exact export formats and retention SLAs.
[04:49] Ruth Park: Walk me through a failure mode: if Dedicated is saturated, what's the fallback?
[04:53] Priya Nair: We support multi-tier routing: primary Dedicated, fallback to compatible hosted model variant if capacity is exceeded. You can set automatic fallback policies that route to cheaper/fallback models with SLA trade-offs.
[05:04] Marcus Cole: So we'd prefer Dedicated with fallback to Hosted rather than Private if it simplifies ops, but again, data residency is the blocker.
[05:10] Jordan Ellis: Understood. One option is to keep PII processing in Private/Dedicated inside your VPC and run non-sensitive workloads in Hosted for cost efficiency.
[05:19] Naoki Sato: About benchmarks — what do you need from us to run them?
[05:23] Priya Nair: We'll need a 24h sample of request logs (anonymized), a representative prompt set (200-500 prompts covering short/long flows), success metrics (what counts as correct), and target traffic profile (base/peak RPS, burst frequency). We'll provide a harness that replays requests at scale and collects p50/p95/p99, tokens/s, and per-request cost estimate.
[05:45] Lena Ortiz: We'll prepare the prompt set and the scoring oracle.
[05:48] Marcus Cole: Timeline wise — we want to make a go/no-go decision in 5-6 weeks. Is that realistic?
[05:54] Jordan Ellis: Yes — typical POC is 4-6 weeks. Week 1 onboarding and runbook, week 2-3 benchmarks, week 4 analysis + decision. If any infra work is needed for Private, it may extend by 1-2 weeks.
[06:06] Ruth Park: What about cost modeling? We need a clear demo of unit economics.
[06:10] Priya Nair: We'll deliver a cost worksheet showing per-token and per-hour estimates for each mode, including amortized GPU costs for Dedicated and ops uplift for Private. That will be part of the pricing pack Jordan sends.
[06:20] Naoki Sato: Are there any gotchas for our GCP setup?
[06:24] Priya Nair: Mostly egress patterns and network latency to Redwood endpoints. For Dedicated and Private we can colocate in your VPC region. Also confirm kernel/quantization compatibility if you plan to use int8 quantization — we'll recommend model/quantization profiles.
[06:39] Marcus Cole: Competitors — we've talked to BigCloud AI and RapidServe. Our main concern is cost and vendor lock-in.
[06:45] Jordan Ellis: Totally. We can show a migration playbook — same API surface, model pinning, and exportable artifacts to reduce lock-in.
[06:53] Ruth Park: Ok, last question on observability — we need token-level breakouts and per-route dashboards.
[06:59] Priya Nair: Redwood Console provides token-level cost, per-model latency histograms, traces, and alerting. We can add custom dashboards for your routes.
[07:08] Marcus Cole: Great.
[07:10] Jordan Ellis: Let's recap and make sure we captured next steps: Jordan to send pricing, Priya to share benchmark harness and runbook link, Naoki to provide logs, Lena to provide prompt set, and we'll schedule the infra deep-dive. Anything else?
[07:24] Marcus Cole: Please include SOC2 and encryption docs.
[07:26] Jordan Ellis: Will do. We'll attach: Redwood POC runbook (link: drive/redwood-poc-runbook.pdf), Performance profiles per model (link: docs/redwood-performance.pdf), SOC2 + ISO pack (link: security/redwood-soc2.zip), KMS integration guide (link: security/kms-guide.pdf).
[07:43] Lena Ortiz: One minor note: when you say p95 includes network, we need clarity on what is in our control vs Redwood's.
[07:49] Priya Nair: We'll provide measurement guidance — synthetic tests from your VPC into our endpoints and a Redwood-collected telemetry set; the decision gate will call out "end-to-end including agreed network path".
[07:59] Naoki Sato: Ok thanks.
[08:01] Jordan Ellis: Great. We'll follow up with the packet. Thanks everyone — we'll target that infra deep-dive next week.

End of transcript.
